answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by pricing each identity: a new key must burn non-refundable compute and post a stake before it can act, and its influence grows only through peer-attested work, never by key count. A forger's fleet therefore pays real cost per node and starts cold, unable to inherit history from an invented fable. Influence tracks earned attestations, so an ocean of cheap keys buys no extra vote: the zenith of power stays with verified work.
